thesis: Intel is down 34.6% over the 60-day window and about 35% below its 52-week high. The dominant disclosed catalyst is an equity raise that was upsized twice — reporting describes an initial $15B target lifted to $20B and ultimately raised as roughly $23B — which is a completed, company-level dilutive event rather than an operating disappointment. Coverage attributes the rest of the decline to profit-taking after a large prior rally and to the sector-wide de-risking of high-beta AI names on Aug 18. No Q2 operating figure was confirmed in this run's sources, so this thesis makes no claim about a beat or a miss. Bank of America's constructive view on the foundry strategy is analyst opinion, not a disclosed result, and is not treated as evidence here. The read is that a confirmed, large dilution event is the identifiable driver and there is no confirmed company-specific offset, which suggests waiting rather than adding.
invalidation: a disclosed external foundry customer commitment or an operating result that shows the raised capital converting into contracted demand

thesis: Coherent is down 31.8% over the 60-day window. Two company-disclosed figures from the Aug 12 fiscal-Q4 report point opposite ways and both belong in the read: reported EPS of $1.74 against a $1.58 consensus (a beat) alongside record quarterly revenue, versus fiscal-2026 operating cash flow down 87% to $79.5 million while AI-optics capacity expansion drove capital expenditure to $1.10 billion. The stock fell about 4-8% after the print and had already dropped roughly 14% on Aug 10 on pre-earnings profit-taking. So the earnings themselves were good on the income statement and poor on cash conversion, and the market has been trading the second of those. That is genuinely offsetting evidence this run cannot settle: whether the capex cycle is an investment in booked AI-optics demand or an outrunning of it is exactly the question the disclosed numbers leave open.
invalidation: operating cash flow recovering toward the level of reported earnings, or a disclosed multi-year optics supply agreement that underwrites the $1.1B capex

thesis: SanDisk is down 29.6% over the 60-day window but the sources read this run identify no memory-specific bad news behind it. The decline is described as profit-taking against an extraordinary run — the stock was up roughly 653% year-to-date entering Aug 18 — compounded by a broad high-beta tech drawdown and a Wall Street Journal report on roughly $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet AI commitments across nine large tech companies, which knocked memory names together (SanDisk, Micron, Western Digital all fell that day). This is a mechanical and sentiment-driven repricing of a crowded position rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration, and no company-disclosed figure from this run's research supports or contradicts it either way. Analyst targets moved in both directions (JPMorgan reinstated Overweight at $2,250; Wells Fargo cut to $1,400), which is opinion rather than evidence.
invalidation: a disclosed NAND pricing or contract datapoint that reframes the move as fundamental in either direction

thesis: Corning is down 27.8% over the 60-day window and 44% below its 52-week high. The disclosed facts cut both ways. Q2, reported Jul 28, beat consensus on revenue and earnings, and Optical Communications — the AI-linked segment — grew 32% year over year to $2.07 billion. Against that, third-quarter guidance came in below elevated consensus and triggered a single-session drop reported at more than 20%, the optical growth rate decelerated from 36% in the prior quarter, and shares fell again on reports that Apple scrapped a planned all-glass anniversary iPhone that would have used the company's specialty glass. A beat paired with light guidance, a decelerating growth segment and a cancelled customer program is offsetting rather than net-positive evidence, and this run cannot resolve which dominates.
invalidation: Q3 optical revenue re-accelerating, or a disclosed replacement design win offsetting the cancelled Apple program

thesis: Rocket Lab is down 27.3% over the 60-day window and 52% below its 52-week high. Q2, reported Aug 10, was mixed in the company's own disclosure: revenue of $234.06 million came in slightly above the ~$232.06 million consensus, but the adjusted loss of $0.08 per share was wider than the $0.06 expected, and management guided GAAP gross margin to 29-31% against roughly 37.6% expected. The company also pushed the Neutron medium-lift reusable rocket's first launch back to later in 2026. Shares fell about 7% after hours and another 8% pre-market. A revenue beat sitting against a margin guide roughly eight points below expectations and a slipped launch date is unresolved evidence — it suggests the top line is scaling while unit economics and the Neutron schedule, the two things the equity story rests on, have both moved the wrong way.
invalidation: a firm Neutron launch date holding, or gross margin guidance returning toward the mid-30s

thesis: Nebius triggered on a 22.4% 60-day decline, but the two disclosed events inside that window point in opposite directions and the more recent one is dilutive. Q2, reported Aug 12, beat: revenue grew 454% year over year, EPS of -$0.12 against -$0.82 expected, AI Cloud up 514%, and full-year guidance of $3.0-3.4 billion was reaffirmed; the stock rose about 28% on it. Then on Aug 19 the company announced a proposed $4.5 billion convertible note offering to fund its data-center build-out and the stock fell roughly 10-14%, with reporting noting the raise covers about 80% of a single quarter's AI spending. That landed alongside a 30-year Treasury yield at 5.33%, a 19-year high, which raises the financing cost of exactly this business model. A confirmed pending convertible raise is a dilution risk, and it arrived on top of an already capital-hungry structure.
invalidation: the convertible offering pricing on terms the market absorbs without further de-rating, or disclosed contracted revenue that pre-funds the build-out

thesis: Micron is down 19.6% over the 60-day window. This run's sources attribute the drop to profit-taking against a roughly 255% year-to-date gain rather than to any memory-specific disclosure, triggered by a Wall Street Journal report on roughly $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet AI commitments across nine major tech companies and compounded by rising long-term yields. That is a sector-wide, sentiment-driven repricing, not a company event. One company-specific item did surface: Netlist filed an ITC complaint on Aug 12 alleging infringement of four patents tied to DDR5 RDIMM and MRDIMM products. This run did not confirm any scheduled hearing, ruling or compliance date for that complaint within the next 90 days, so it is noted here rather than flagged. No Micron-disclosed quarterly figure was verified this run, so no claim is made about the last print.
invalidation: an ITC procedural schedule that puts a DDR5-related decision inside the next quarter, or a disclosed HBM contract change

thesis: SpaceX is down 13.3% over the 60-day window and 41% below its 52-week high. Its first report since the June IPO, on Aug 4, beat on both lines the sources state: revenue of $7.81 billion against $6.93 billion expected and a loss of $0.09 per share against $0.26 expected. The stock nonetheless fell about 8% in extended trading because capital expenditure jumped more than sixfold year over year to $18.37 billion in the quarter, $15.83 billion of it in AI. Nvidia disclosed a $21 billion stake as of quarter-end. The beat and the capex figure are both company-disclosed and they offset: revenue is running ahead of expectations while the spend required to produce it is scaling far faster, and that spend is being repriced right now by a 30-year Treasury yield at a 19-year high. This run cannot settle which side dominates.
invalidation: capital expenditure decelerating relative to revenue, or disclosed contracted backlog that underwrites the AI spend

thesis: AST SpaceMobile is down 11.1% over the 60-day window and 51% below its 52-week high. Q2, reported Aug 10, missed on both lines: revenue of $31.52 million against $34.98 million expected (though up from $1.16 million a year earlier) and EPS of -$0.35 against -$0.29 expected. Against that, the company affirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150-200 million, reported roughly $1.30 billion of contracted commercial revenue and government awards in backlog, and successfully launched BlueBird satellites 11, 12 and 13 on Aug 5 — the largest communications arrays deployed in low Earth orbit. So execution on hardware and backlog is real while the current quarter came in short, and hitting the affirmed full-year range now requires a steep second-half ramp. That tension is unresolved on the evidence read this run.
invalidation: Q3 revenue tracking to the affirmed $150-200M full-year range, or a further guidance affirmation missed

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics triggered on a 24.6% 60-day decline that sits oddly against its own disclosures. Q2, reported Aug 6, was a fifth consecutive record quarter: revenue up 86% year over year to $191.9 million and adjusted EPS of $0.06 against $0.01 expected, with Q3 guided to $255-290 million of revenue and $0.11-0.26 adjusted EPS, and management stating AI, cloud and CATV demand should exceed capacity through at least mid-2027. A reported draft FCC ban on new Chinese optical transceivers is an additional, still-draft tailwind. The stock ran to roughly $155 on Aug 17 and then gave back about 17% in three sessions alongside the broad AI-infrastructure drawdown on 19-year-high long-term yields. The counter-case is that the guidance predates that repricing and the FCC rule is not final; the read here is that the disclosed demand commentary spans multiple quarters rather than the two sessions that moved the price, but with a draft rule and a pre-selloff guide both in the mix, no single factor is cleanly dominant.
invalidation: Q3 revenue landing below the guided $255M floor, or the FCC transceiver proposal being dropped

thesis: Marvell triggered on an 18.5% 60-day decline measured from a late-June level, but the recent direction is the opposite: the stock ran from a $163.40 close on Jul 29 into the $230s-$240s. The specific, already-signed catalyst is a disclosed commercial agreement granting Alphabet a warrant to buy roughly 58.97 million shares — about 7% of shares outstanding — at an exercise price of $206.58, on which the stock rose 8.2%. The company also launched Bravera SC6 SSD controllers, Structera X CXL memory expansion and Photonic Fabric, with Bravera sampling expected in Q4, and the reported FCC action on Chinese optical transceivers steers data-center demand toward non-Chinese suppliers. The clear counter-case is that the Alphabet warrant is itself roughly 7% dilution, which the market has so far treated as the price of the commercial relationship rather than a cost. That is not settled either way, and Q2 fiscal-2027 earnings on Aug 27 is an unresolved binary event that could reverse the read within days.
invalidation: the Aug 27 print showing the Alphabet relationship is not converting into disclosed revenue, or the warrant terms being repriced

thesis: AMD is down 14.9% over the 60-day window and about 20% below its 52-week high, on its third consecutive down session. The company-disclosed side is strong: Q2 EPS of $1.66 and revenue of $11.55 billion both beat, with data-center growth reported at 107%. The decline, though, is attributed by this run's sources to factors outside the company — a sector-wide semiconductor selloff on AI-overspend fears, surging Treasury yields hitting the most aggressively valued AI names (AMD's trailing P/E is cited at 123 against a ~35 sector average), terms for a planned $4.75 billion debt sale, and a report that DeepSeek is developing its own AI processor. Because the move is sector-driven and valuation-driven rather than a response to anything AMD disclosed, this is a low-conviction read: the fundamentals verified this run have not deteriorated, but nothing company-specific explains or arrests the drawdown either. The $4.75B sale is debt, not equity, so no dilution flag is raised.
invalidation: a disclosed data-center order or guidance change, or the DeepSeek in-house silicon report being confirmed with a named customer loss

thesis: TSMC is down 11.05% over the 60-day window and 13% below its 52-week high — the shallowest drawdown of any name that triggered this cycle. The company-disclosed datapoint in the window is monthly revenue: July revenue rose 44.7% year over year to NT$467.58 billion, taking the first seven months to NT$2.87 trillion, up 37%. The decline is attributed to a broad semiconductor selloff (shares fell 4.1% on Aug 18 as the sector sold off together), a premium valuation with a trailing P/E above 28x against a five-year median of 22.8x, and geopolitical and export-control concerns. Management has also cautioned that scaling overseas production in Arizona and Japan could compress consolidated gross margins by 2 to 4 percentage points — a company-disclosed negative that sits directly against the revenue growth. The move is sector-wide rather than company-specific, which is what caps this read.
invalidation: monthly revenue growth decelerating materially, or the overseas gross-margin dilution landing at the high end of the disclosed 2-4 point range

thesis: Held position, re-thesised fresh. The catalyst is a completed, company-disclosed result: fiscal Q4 2026, reported Jul 29, with revenue of $90.01 billion (up 18% year over year) against $87.62 billion consensus and adjusted EPS of $4.74 against $4.24 expected. Azure and other cloud services grew 43%, accelerating from 40% the prior quarter, and Azure crossed $100 billion of annual revenue for the first time; Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats with net additions more than doubling sequentially. The stock rose about 8% after hours and roughly 17% the following session, which is the bulk of the 31% 60-day move. The strongest counter-evidence is that the quarter included a $3.2 billion gain from the Anthropic investment, so the EPS beat is not purely operating. That does not change the read, because the two figures the thesis rests on — Azure's 43% growth and the $100 billion annual run-rate — are segment revenue measures that the investment gain cannot flatter. A securities class action covering May 2025-Jan 2026 alleges earlier Copilot and Azure-capacity statements were misleading; its lead-plaintiff deadline was Aug 11, 2026 and this run found no scheduled ruling, hearing or trial date in the next 90 days, and its class period closes before this quarter's disclosures. Shares sit 12.5% below the 52-week high.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerating back below 40%, or Copilot paid-seat additions failing to compound in the next quarterly disclosure
sources: Microsoft Investor Relations FY26 Q4 press release: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2026-q4/press-release-webcast

thesis: Held position, re-thesised fresh. CORT is the only name up over the window — 51.9% in 60 days — and it closed within 1% of its 52-week high. The catalysts are confirmed and company-disclosed: Q2 results on Jul 29 reported at $256.1 million of revenue with 2026 guidance raised, and the commercial ramp of Lifyorli (relacorilant), FDA-approved in March 2026 with nab-paclitaxel for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, which lifted second-half expectations and drove a 27% single-session gain on Jul 30 on roughly five times normal volume. The company has also resubmitted the relacorilant NDA for Cushing's syndrome, with an FDA decision set for Dec 17, 2026. The strongest counter-evidence is that this is the same molecule whose Cushing's Complete Response Letter on Dec 31, 2025 cut the stock roughly in half in a day and produced a still-active securities class action (Allegheny County Employees' Retirement System v. Corcept, N.D. Cal.). That does not change the current read: the revenue and raised guidance now in hand come from the approved ovarian-cancer indication, which is independent of the Cushing's decision, and the class period ends Dec 30, 2025, before any of these disclosures. This run found no scheduled ruling, hearing or trial date in that case within the next 90 days, so no litigation flag is raised — but the Dec 17 PDUFA is a real binary event further out.
invalidation: Lifyorli revenue failing to sustain the raised 2026 guidance, or the Dec 17 Cushing's decision arriving early as another Complete Response Letter

thesis: Held position, re-thesised fresh. Astera Labs is down 33.9% over the 60-day window and 42% below its 52-week high, yet its own disclosures inside that window were strong: Q2, reported Aug 4, delivered record revenue of $392.4 million, up 27% sequentially and 104% year over year on AI fabric and signal-conditioning demand, with Scorpio X-Series entering volume production and Q3 revenue guided to $540-560 million. The counter-case is that the stock has fallen about 12% since that report and kept falling with the rest of the AI-infrastructure complex as long-term yields hit 19-year highs — meaning the market is repricing the durability of AI capex rather than disputing the quarter. Two live factors, neither of which this run can establish as dominant: a company-disclosed guide implying another large sequential step-up, against an external cost-of-capital shift that hits the customers funding that step-up. Analyst actions were positive into the drawdown (Jefferies to $450, Northland upgrade to Buy at $350) but that is opinion, not evidence. The position still supports holding on the disclosed numbers; it does not support adding on them alone.
invalidation: Q3 revenue landing below the guided $540M floor, or a disclosed hyperscaler capex deferral naming PCIe/AI-fabric programs

thesis: Held position, re-thesised fresh; no Step 2 signal fired (60-day move 3.8%, volume 0.52x, 15.3% below the 52-week high), so this thesis exists because the position is held, not because a signal triggered. The disclosed facts remain strong: fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $43,842 million rose 87.5% year over year and beat consensus by roughly 23%, adjusted EPS of $4.86 beat by roughly 64%, and management raised full-year revenue guidance toward $167 billion with about $60 billion of AI server revenue expected. Dell closed at a record on Aug 4 after being named technology provider on a $10 billion AI-factory project in Norway. The counter-case is that the stock has given back about 6.6% from that record as the whole AI hardware complex de-rated on financing costs, and that AI-server revenue carries lower margins than Dell's traditional mix — a tension this run cannot settle from the sources read. Decisively, the next quarterly report lands on Sep 1, 2026, an unresolved binary event roughly twelve days out that could reverse the read, which is what holds this at medium regardless of how strong the last print was.
invalidation: the Sep 1 report walking back the ~$167B full-year revenue guidance or the ~$60B AI server figure, or AI-server gross margin compressing below the level implied by that guide
